question: A 63-year-old woman comes to the emergency department because of a 1-day history of progressive blurring and darkening of her vision in the right eye. Upon waking up in the morning, she suddenly started seeing multiple dark streaks. She has migraines and type 2 diabetes mellitus diagnosed at her last health maintenance examination 20 years ago. She has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 40 years. Her only medication is sumatriptan. Her vitals are within normal limits. Ophthalmologic examination shows visual acuity of 20/40 in the left eye and 20/100 in the right eye. The fundus is obscured and difficult to visualize on fundoscopic examination of the right eye. The red reflex is diminished on the right. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Progressive blurring and darkening of vision in the right eye" -> "Sudden onset of multiple dark streaks in the morning" -> "Obscured fundus and diminished red reflex on the right eye" -> "Central retinal vein occlusion" -> 80% CHAIN: "Visual acuity of 20/100 in the right eye" -> "Difficult visualization of the fundus on the right eye" -> "Diminished red reflex on the right" -> "Central retinal vein occlusion" -> 75% CHAIN: "History of migraines and type 2 diabetes mellitus" -> "Long-term smoking history" -> "Sumatriptan use" -> "Increased risk for vascular occlusive events" -> "Central retinal vein occlusion" -> 80%
enhanced_information: The most likely diagnosis for the 63-year-old woman with progressive blurring and darkening of vision in the right eye, sudden onset of dark streaks, obscured fundus, and diminished red reflex is Central retinal vein occlusion. This is supported by the visual acuity of 20/100 in the right eye, difficulty visualizing the fundus, and the patient's history of migraines, type 2 diabetes mellitus, long-term smoking, and sumatriptan use, all of which increase the risk for vascular occlusive events.
analysis: The most likely diagnosis for the 63-year-old woman with progressive blurring and darkening of vision in the right eye, sudden onset of dark streaks, obscured fundus, and diminished red reflex is Central retinal vein occlusion. This is supported by the visual acuity findings, difficulty visualizing the fundus, and the patient's risk factors such as migraines, type 2 diabetes mellitus, long-term smoking, and sumatriptan use, all of which predispose to vascular occlusive events.
